# git: extend git flow to use it tactically

Rethink the per-repository git flow ([git_flow](../../bin/git_flow), [git_start](../../bin/git_start), [git_stop](../../bin/git_stop)) in the light of three articles on small, deliberate commits and review-light integration:

- [Use Git tactically](https://stackoverflow.blog/2022/04/06/use-git-tactically/) (Stack Overflow blog): commit as a checkpoint tool, reshape history before sharing;
- [Git organized: a better git flow](https://render.com/blog/git-organized-a-better-git-flow) (Render): work first, then stage and commit in logical pieces (`reset`, `add -p`);
- [Ship / Show / Ask](https://martinfowler.com/articles/ship-show-ask.html) (Martin Fowler): choose per change whether to merge directly, merge and announce, or ask for review.

The flow today is branch-per-issue with `progress` commits and a `done` that rebases and force-pushes; the ticket is about which of these practices the aliases should encode. Part of the "Git flow" milestone.
